# Public FAQ

## Is this an official ICFP Programming Contest release?

No. Afterimage is an independent clean-room programming-puzzle work. It is not
affiliated with the ICFP Programming Contest or its organizers.

## Is it a remake of ICFPC 2006?

No. It pursues comparable scope and a single world-spanning conceptual spine,
but uses a different story, computational substrate, puzzle vocabulary,
formats, and mechanics.

## What do I need to run it?

Python 3.11 or newer. The player kit uses only the standard library and does
not require a network connection.

## Do all four languages contain the same problems?

Yes. English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, and German are external
presentation packs for the same immutable bundle. Case IDs, answer schemas,
verification, scoring, witnesses, and receipts do not change with locale.

## Is this a collection of unrelated puzzles?

No. All eight families operate on the same causal event world. Different
families ask participants to intervene, reconstruct, program, map, synchronize,
synthesize, or audit that shared world.

## Does correctness require an optimized solution?

No. A valid solution receives completion credit and unlocks. Optimization
improves score but does not gate the story.

## Does the kit send telemetry?

No telemetry is enabled by default. The public kit is offline. The optional
playtest telemetry path is separate, consent-gated, and does not store solution
content.

## Are solutions or author witnesses included?

No. The public player and engine packages exclude author witnesses, private
baselines, case sources, author golden data, and authoring tools.

## Can media show the ending?

Please use the spoiler guide. The key art and supplied screenshots reveal the
premise and two-history motif without revealing a final witness or solution.
